data.title: Binance restores withdrawals across nearly all networks four weeks after record $6.3B hack
data.description:
Binance says withdrawals are running again on nearly all of its supported networks. The restart comes roughly four weeks after attackers drained approximately $6.3 billion to $6.4 billion from the exchange's hot wallets, the largest crypto theft on record.

A small number of networks are still temporarily suspended. Binance says those pauses are for maintenance or planned upgrades unrelated to the hack.

The breach took place on October 29, 2026. Funds left the exchange across multiple blockchains in roughly 20 to 30 minutes, and Bitcoin and Ethereum took the heaviest hits.

Binance halted withdrawals quickly. It reopened them in stages, starting on November 1 with Bitcoin.

From there, the rollout widened network by network. By November 14, 2026, 87 networks were operational again, and most services were restored by late November.

Binance also sped up its proof-of-reserves process. Proof of reserves is a public accounting exercise meant to show that an exchange holds enough assets to cover customer deposits.

Binance pledged to make customers whole. The exchange committed over $6.34 billion to restore affected assets and set a target of completing reimbursement by November 12, 2026.

The money came from three sources: the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), the company's corporate treasury, and surplus from its futures insurance fund.

Binance has said no customer would bear losses from the incident.

Working with authorities, Binance helped freeze or intercept roughly $2.82 billion to $2.85 billion of the stolen assets, mostly stablecoins such as USDT and USDC.

The Department of Justice obtained court orders covering over $1.2 billion of the frozen funds. As of late November, though, only about $32 million had actually been recovered.

The attack has been attributed to TraderTraitor, a hacking group linked to North Korea. The attackers rapidly compromised Binance's internal systems, which let them withdraw across several chains at once.

Binance said it worked with the FBI and the US Secret Service on the investigation. The stablecoin freezes depended on that cooperation, since they required fast coordination between the exchange, token issuers and authorities.

For Binance customers, the immediate point is that balances were covered and access has largely returned.

The freeze and recovery numbers are worth tracking. With about $2.82 billion to $2.85 billion frozen but only around $32 million returned as of late November, the rate at which court orders turn into recovered assets will show whether law enforcement cooperation can meaningfully reduce losses from major hacks.

The remaining suspended networks are the last open question. Binance says their downtime has nothing to do with the hack.

data.title: Binance completes withdrawal recovery four weeks after $6.3B hack
data.description:
Binance said Thursday it had lifted all withdrawal suspensions related to its October hack, four weeks after an attack drained $6.3 billion in funds from the exchange in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.

In an announcement, Binance said withdrawals had resumed across nearly all networks, with a small number remaining temporarily suspended due to maintenance or planned upgrades unrelated to the hack.

The exchange’s network status page shows partial deposit and withdrawal suspensions for several cryptocurrencies. USDC withdrawals, for instance, remain suspended on Hedera and World Chain due to low hot wallet balances and on Sonic due to security issues.

Binance warned users against phishing attempts, saying it would never request passwords or seed phrases or offer expedited withdrawals. The exchange also said customers could verify that their assets are backed at a minimum ratio of 1:1 through its proof-of-reserves system.

The Oct. 29 attack targeted Binance’s hot wallets across multiple blockchains, with blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs attributing the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Following the breach, Binance said it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the losses.

Thursday’s announcement marks the end of a phased recovery process that began on Nov. 1, when Binance resumed Bitcoin withdrawals before gradually restoring services across other blockchain networks.

data.title: France's Macron says Le Pen should be less arrogant after she criticises EU budget talks
data.description:
By Michel Rose

French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that far-right leader Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner in the 2027 presidential election, should be more humble after she criticised efforts to reach a deal on the EU’s next long-term budget before the vote.

The personal criticism of Le Pen was an unusual step for Macron, who typically refrains from commenting on domestic French politics while in Brussels with other EU leaders.

“Mrs Le Pen is campaigning,” Macron said. “It takes a peculiar kind of arrogance to think she’s already in charge of France’s destiny. Last I checked, she wasn’t elected.”

Le Pen earlier on Thursday accused the European Commission and Macron of trying to rush through a budget deal before the French election.

“The apparent aim is to deter us from defending France’s interests in EU budget negotiations if the French people entrust us with the responsibility of governing,” she said in a post on X.

“Our leaders should get to work putting (France) back on its feet instead of resorting to cheap political manoeuvres to prevent the French people from making their voices heard at the ballot box.”

Macron said that he was careful to take into account the presidential election and that if there was no deal by December 31, negotiations would have to resume in the second half of 2027, when his successor would be in office. But he added Le Pen should not act as if she already was France's president, and that he would continue to do his job until the end of his term in May 2027.

“You have to be more humble when you’re campaigning, even if you already see yourself in the job,” Macron said.

data.title: Psyched Wellness Provides Strategic Review Update
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Psyched Wellness Ltd. (OTCID: PSYCF) (FSE: 5U9) ("Psyched Wellness" or the "Company"), a life sciences company focused on the production and distribution of health and wellness products derived from the Amanita Muscaria mushroom, provides an update on its previously announced strategic review and its ongoing financing requirements.

Further to its news release dated July 29, 2026, the Company continues to pursue and evaluate strategic alternatives. These alternatives may include debt or equity financing, strategic partnerships, the sale of some or all of the Company's assets or business operations, a merger or other business combination, or a combination of these alternatives.

Gotham Green Partners and its affiliated funds (collectively, "GGP"), which have historically provided financial support to the Company, are not expected to provide further financing. As a result, the Company is pursuing alternative financing arrangements and strategic opportunities to address its working capital requirements and support its ongoing operations.

The Board and management remain focused on evaluating available alternatives with the objective of preserving shareholder value. The Company's ability to continue funding its operations will depend on securing additional financing or completing a strategic transaction that provides sufficient liquidity. If these efforts are unsuccessful, the Company may need to further reduce or curtail its operations.

There is no established timeline for completion of the strategic review. There can be no assurance that additional financing will be available on acceptable terms, or at all, or that the strategic review will result in a transaction or any particular outcome. Any proposed transaction may be subject to applicable regulatory, shareholder and other approvals.

data.title: Imaging Dynamics Company Ltd. Announces Related Party Transactions
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Imaging Dynamics Company Ltd. (the "Company") today announces that in the period beginning March 6, 2019 and ending on November 9, 2026, the Company entered into certain loan agreements with certain directors, related parties and Control Persons (as such term is defined in TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV") Policy 1.1 - Interpretation) of the Company, pursuant to which the Company was advanced certain amounts of debt by such directors and Control Persons (collectively, the "Debt Transactions"). These related party transactions may refer as non-arm's length transactions. The proceeds of the Debt Transactions were used to fund the Company's ongoing operations and for general corporate commercial purposes. Through inadvertence, the Company did not publicly disseminate the details of the Debt Transactions at the time such Debt Transactions were completed.

The Debt Transactions consisted of transactions among the Company and certain directors and Control Persons of the Company. Paul Lin, a director of the Company, advanced three installments of principal pursuant to the terms of certain promissory notes issued by the Company as follows: (i) on March 6, 2019, Mr. Lin advanced a principal amount of USD$71,073; (ii) on August 27, 2019, Mr. Lin advanced a principal amount of CAD$31,001.60; and (iii) on March 13, 2020, Mr. Lin advanced a principal amount of CAD$27,200.00 (such advances collectively referenced as the "Lin Transactions"). The amounts advanced to the Company pursuant to the Lin Transactions are non-interest bearing, unsecured obligations of the Company, payable on demand.

Tim Seung, a director of the Company, advanced three installments of principal pursuant to the terms of certain promissory notes issued by the Company as follows: (i) on February 14, 2020, Mr. Seung advanced a principal amount of CAD$26,254.00; (ii) on March 31, 2021, Mr. Seung advanced a principal amount of CAD$62,003.20; and (iii) on June 30, 2022, Mr. Seung advanced a principal amount of CAD$41,252.88 (such advances collectively referenced as the "Seung Transactions"). The amounts advanced to the Company pursuant to the Seung Transactions are non-interest bearing, unsecured obligations of the Company, payable on demand.

The amount of principal advanced to the Company pursuant to the Lin Transactions and the Seung Transactions remain outstanding and payable obligations of the Company. The Company has not repaid any amounts owing by it to Mr. Lin and Mr. Seung pursuant to the Lin Transactions and the Seung Transactions, respectively.

New Journey Health Group Ltd. ("New Journey") holds 40.86% of the issued and outstanding shares of the Company; by virtue of its shareholdings, it is a Control Person as defined under the policies of the TSXV. On November 21, 2022, and subsequently thereafter until October 31, 2025, New Journey advanced certain amounts of principal to the Company (the "New Journey Transactions") pursuant to the terms and conditions of a loan agreement and ancillary promissory note documentation entered into by and among the Company and New Journey (collectively, the "New Journey Documentation"). Pursuant to the terms of the New Journey Documentation, the term of each advance of principal matures on the earlier of: (a) five years from the date of the advance; or (b) the date a resolution is passed to dissolve New Journey. Interest accrues on the principal amounts at 6% for the duration of the term of such advance. As at October 31, 2026, the Company is indebted to New Journey pursuant to the New Journey Transactions in the aggregate amount of USD$2,182,736.90 (CAD$3,047,100.71).

On January 1, 2020, and subsequently thereafter until September 16, 2022, Hua Star Capital USA LLC ("Hua Star") advanced certain amounts of principal to the Company (the "Hua Star Transactions") pursuant to the terms and conditions of a loan agreement and ancillary promissory note documentation entered into by and among the Company and Hua Star (collectively, the "Hua Star Documentation"). Hua Star is a related party of the Company as it is controlled by Mr. Seung, a director of the Company. Pursuant to the terms of the Hua Star Documentation, the term of each advance of principal matures on the earlier of: (a) five years from the date of the advance; or (b) the date a resolution is passed to dissolve Hua Star. Interest accrues on the principal amounts at 6% for the duration of the term of such advance. As of October 31, 2026, the Company is indebted to Hua Star pursuant to the Hua Star Transactions in the aggregate amount of USD$1,498,000.00 (CAD$2,091,208.00).

As of October 31, 2026, the company has not paid out any interest accrued to New Journey on the amount of USD$484,531.40 (CAD $676,405.83) and to Hua Star on the amount of USD$300,021.50 (CAD $418,830.01). The company estimates it would borrow up to USD$410,000.00 in promissory notes from New Journey in the next 12 months.

Exchange rate used in translation of USD amount to CAD amounts is 1.396 on October 30, 2026, published on bank of Canada website.

Following notification of the delayed disclosure of the Debt Transactions by the TSXV, the Company has been working diligently to provide the required disclosure to its shareholders and to the TSXV in respect of the Debt Transactions. The Company continues to undertake to provide the necessary and timely disclosure of its material business activities, as required by the policies of the TSXV.

data.title: US, Qatar to help Venezuela clear regional development bank arrears, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Venezuela in arrears with regional development banks IDB, CAF
  • Bridge loans from US to clear IDB arrears, Qatar seen aiding with CAF
  • Total arrears to both development lenders are about $4.16 billion

By Rodrigo Campos, Libby George, Mayela Armas and Cassandra Garrison

Venezuela is working on separate bridge loans with the US Treasury and Qatar to clear arrears owed to two regional development banks, a move that could unlock fresh multilateral financing for the cash-strapped country, four people familiar with the discussions said.

The unusual arrangements would allow Venezuela to settle arrears that currently prevent the lenders from extending fresh credit, reopening a potentially important source of funding as the government seeks to revive the economy and re-engage with international financial institutions after years of US sanctions.

Under one arrangement, the US Treasury would provide a bridge loan to clear Venezuela’s arrears to the Inter-American Development Bank, the people said. Two of the people said the funds would come via the Treasury's Exchange Stabilization Fund.

Caracas said in a document it owed the IDB $2.74 billion in principal and interest as of the end of 2025.

The US Treasury did not reply to a request for comment and the IDB declined to comment.

Two people familiar with the discussions likened the transaction to an overnight loan: Treasury funds would clear the arrears, allowing the IDB to approve new lending, whose proceeds could then be used to repay the United States. Venezuela would ultimately remain responsible for the debt.

The IDB cannot lend into arrears, but is already discussing possible loans that could be approved after the arrears are cleared, two of the people said.

One person said an initial operation under consideration would be made through the IDB’s Special Development Lending window and would exceed its $500 million cap, requiring a waiver. A second waiver would be needed because Venezuela does not currently have an International Monetary Fund programme.

SDL loans carry some of the IDB’s costliest terms, the person said.

BRIDGE FROM QATAR

Separately, Qatar is considering a bridge loan to help Venezuela clear arrears owed to CAF, the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean, two people said.

Venezuela reported owing CAF $1.42 billion at the end of 2025.

Acting President Delcy Rodriguez said in early November that Venezuela was negotiating with multilateral institutions over about $17 billion in public- and private-sector financing. On Tuesday, however, she put potential funding at $10 billion, without explaining the change.

The Venezuelan communications ministry, which handles all media queries for the government, did not respond to a request for comment.

CAF declined to comment, and Qatar's government did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Calixto Ortega, Rodriguez's top economic adviser, said on state television on Tuesday that the government was in “advanced discussions” to clear its arrears with multilateral lenders, without adding details.

Ruling party lawmaker Ramon Lobo, part of the National Assembly's economics committee, told a session on Thursday the country was seeking bridge loans to clear arrears with multilateral lenders, though he offered no further details.

"With those resources, these bridge loans, we will settle what we have overdue with these multilateral organizations. And those multilateral organizations will immediately grant us a loan so that we can pay back the country that provided those resources," Lobo said. "The bridge loan will allow a country with whom we are in talks to provide us resources."

Venezuela this week put its public-sector liabilities at $237.5 billion at the end of 2025, equivalent to 242% of GDP, including $116.5 billion in commercial debt and $67.3 billion in nonfinancial obligations concentrated in state oil company PDVSA.

data.title: UK is ‘getting it wrong’ on DeFi regulation, says Coinbase
data.description:
Coinbase and Stand With Crypto, a crypto advocacy group backed by the exchange, are pushing back against the UK’s proposed approach to decentralized finance (DeFi), arguing that restrictions on regulated crypto platforms could leave consumers with fewer safeguards when accessing DeFi services.

The criticism follows reports on Nov. 26 that the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) plans to proceed with tighter rules and authorization requirements for DeFi platforms, citing money laundering risks exposed by the $6.3 billion Binance hack. Although the attack targeted a centralized exchange, hackers moved stolen funds through decentralized protocols, complicating efforts to trace and freeze the assets.

Katie Harries, head of policy for Europe at Coinbase, said the proposals could limit opportunities for regulated firms to work with authorities on consumer safeguards.

“The UK is getting its approach to DeFi wrong,” Harries told Cointelegraph. “This isn’t a ban on UK consumers using DeFi; it’s a ban on giving them a regulated route to use it.”

In an October opinion piece for Cointelegraph, Harries argued that the proposed framework could effectively prevent regulated crypto platforms from offering DeFi services, as requirements to execute customer orders through authorized trading venues could exclude decentralized protocols with no central operator capable of obtaining FCA authorization.

UK users could face fewer DeFi options

Harries argued that regulated platforms could help address the FCA’s concerns around DeFi through due diligence and safeguards.

The FCA has previously used regulatory sandboxes to allow financial services firms to test new products in live markets under regulatory oversight. On Feb. 25, the regulator named four regulated entities to test out stablecoin products within its regulatory sandbox.

“The UK has got a lot right on crypto, but its approach is closing the door on DeFi innovation,” Harries said.

Harry Pearce-Gould, general manager at Stand With Crypto, argued that the proposals could leave UK users with fewer options for accessing DeFi services. “That leaves UK crypto users without the trusted, regulated routes to access DeFi that will be available to people doing the same thing in other jurisdictions.”

He said people should be able to use crypto for financial activities such as borrowing against their holdings, provided they have clear information about the associated risks.

UK’s ambitions as a global crypto hub

The implications could extend beyond consumer protection, potentially putting the UK at a competitive disadvantage in the digital asset industry, according to Harries. “The UK is creating a prohibition, and that doesn’t sit right with its ambition to be a global centre for digital assets,” she said.

The FCA closed consultations on its proposed DeFi guidance and wider crypto regulatory framework on Nov. 18, with final guidance expected in January 2027. The new regime is scheduled to take effect on Oct. 25, 2027.

data.title: Resource shares help lift TSX to eight-day high
data.description:
By Sudeshna Ghoshal and Fergal Smith

Canada's main stock index rose to an eight-day high on Thursday, led by gains for energy and metal mining shares, as investors grew optimistic that market volatility would fade.

The S&P/TSX Composite Index ended up 246.89 points, or 0.7%, at 34,426.88, its highest closing level since November 18.

  • Stock markets in Europe and across Asia also rallied as the latest salvo of US tariffs looked less damaging than first feared and after the US Thanksgiving holiday appeared to offer a welcome break from AI jitters

  • "We're coming off quite a lot of volatility over the last week and you're seeing some big moves in commodity markets and the whole AI trade in the US has been quite volatile," said Michael Dehal, a senior portfolio manager at Dehal Investment Partners at Raymond James

  • "We do think that a lot of the excesses in the markets have been washed out and we could be set up for a year-end rally," Dehal said

  • The energy sector added 1.9% after Yemen's Houthis said they hit ​Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery and Iran said mines struck ships in the Strait of Hormuz, boosting the price of oil. US crude futures were up 1.5% at $84.91 a barrel

  • The materials sector , which includes metal mining shares, gained 1.7% as copper prices rebounded on bargain hunting

  • Technology rose 0.9% and industrials (.GSPTTIN) ended 0.6% higher

  • Alimentation Couche-Tard does not plan to raise the price in its public tender offer for Polish convenience store operator Zabka or extend the acceptance period, CEO Alex Miller told Reuters. The company's shares rose 1.9%

data.title: Envipco: Statement on Greek distributor
data.description:
Amersfoort, The Netherlands - 26 November 2026: As reported in the press, the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) is conducting an investigation into recycling kiosks sold by Texan in 2020 to Greek municipalities. Texan is Envipco’s distributor in the Greek market with Envipco selling RVMs and parts to Texan.

Envipco Hellas was today visited by Greek authorities as part of the ongoing EPPO investigation. Envipco has no reason to believe it is a target of the investigation by EPPO and is fully cooperating with the authorities.

Envipco will keep the market informed of any material developments.

José Matthijsse, CEO +31 33 285 1773

Envipco Holding N.V. (Envipco), www.envipco.com, is a Netherlands-based holding company listed on Euronext Amsterdam and Euronext Oslo Børs (Symbols: ENVI/ENVIP). Envipco, with operations in several countries around the globe, is a recognized leader in the development and operation of reverse vending machines (RVMs), automated technological systems for the recovery of used beverage containers. Known for its innovative technology and market leadership, Envipco holds several intellectual property rights for RVM systems, including but not limited to beverage refund deposit markings, material type identification, compaction, and accounting.

data.title: President Trump Says Pre-Election GDP Numbers Were Fake, Seeks Probe On Commerce Department
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - U.S. President Donald Trump has accused the Commerce Department of releasing 'fake' economic growth figures just ahead of the midterm election on November 3 and sought an immediate investigation into the 'grave' matter.

In a post on the social media platform Truth Social, where he wished Thanksgiving, Trump said, 'Additionally, I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late.'

Revised data from the Commerce Department showed on Wednesday that the third quarter gross domestic product growth figure was revised to 4.3 percent from the initially estimated 3.4 percent.

Trump called this 'A record setting error, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated.'

In a post on the same platform earlier on Thursday, Trump said, 'The American Economy under The Trump Administration is doing far better than the good numbers already released.'

The president questioned why the correct number was not released before the election and sought an immediate investigation. 'This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error,' he added.

The Commerce Department routinely revises GDP figures as new and detailed data from various sectors become available and the agency follows its own schedule to release the revised data.

Trump has repeatedly tried to cast doubts on economic indicators that does not favor his administration and is now seeking to put the blame for Republicans' poor performance in the midterm elections on the GDP estimates.
